---
name: init-framework
description: Build Roblox games on KashTheKing's Init module loader (Wally package kashtheking/init, Init Framework Studio plugin), in a Rojo project on disk or directly in Roblox Studio. Use when a game has ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Init or InitServer/InitClient boot scripts, when the user asks to install or set up Init, or to add a Service, Controller, GuiController, Binder, Network (Packet) module, Class or Input context to a game that uses Init.
---

# Init framework

Init is a module loader for Roblox. Two boot scripts (one Script, one LocalScript) call `Init.start`
with a list of folders. Init requires every ModuleScript in them, calls each module's `Init`, then
each module's `Start`, then connects the module's hook methods (`OnPlayerAdded`, `OnHeartbeat`, ...).
Modules are plain tables; they never connect those events themselves.

Docs: https://kashtheking.com/init/ · Source: https://github.com/KashTheKing/init

**Templates** (one file per module type) are in the first of these you can read:
1. `templates/` two folders up from this skill (the Claude Code plugin and the Wally package both have it),
   e.g. `Packages/_Index/kashtheking_init@1.0.1/init/templates/` after `wally install`.
2. The **Templates** section at the end of this file, if it has one.
3. `https://kashtheking.com/init/templates/<File>`, e.g. `.../templates/Service.luau`.

## 1. Find out how the game is set up

- **Files (Rojo)**: there's a `*.project.json`, usually a `wally.toml`. Edit files; go to 2A.
- **Studio**: you have Studio tools (`execute_luau`, `multi_edit`, ...) or you are Roblox Studio's Assistant.
  Create instances; go to 2B.
- **Neither** (a chat with no tools): write the code and say exactly where each script goes. For setup,
  send the user to the plugin (2B).
- **Already uses Init** if `ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Init` exists, a `wally.toml` lists `kashtheking/init`,
  or a script calls `Init.start`. Skip to section 3.
- **Old Init** if `ReplicatedStorage.Init` is a ModuleScript with `SharedEntries`/`ServerEntries`
  children and `InitServer`/`InitClient` scripts inside it. It works; don't migrate unless asked
  (guide: https://kashtheking.com/init/docs/migrating/). Its modules use the same methods.

## 2A. Install in a Rojo project

1. In `wally.toml`, under `[dependencies]`: `Init = "kashtheking/init@1.0.1"`. No `wally.toml` yet? Run
   `wally init` first. Then `wally install`.
2. The project file must put `Packages` in `ReplicatedStorage`. If the project already maps
   ReplicatedStorage, ServerScriptService and StarterPlayerScripts to folders, keep its layout and use those
   folders below. A new project can use:

   ```json
   {
   	"name": "Game",
   	"tree": {
   		"$className": "DataModel",
   		"ReplicatedStorage": { "$path": "src/ReplicatedStorage", "Packages": { "$path": "Packages" } },
   		"ServerScriptService": { "$path": "src/ServerScriptService" },
   		"StarterPlayer": { "StarterPlayerScripts": { "$path": "src/StarterPlayerScripts" } }
   	}
   }
   ```

3. Create the boot scripts and folders (paths for the layout above):

   ```
   src/ServerScriptService/InitServer.server.luau
   src/ServerScriptService/Services/.gitkeep
   src/ServerScriptService/Binders/.gitkeep
   src/StarterPlayerScripts/InitClient.client.luau
   src/ReplicatedStorage/Network/.gitkeep
   src/ReplicatedStorage/Services/.gitkeep
   src/ReplicatedStorage/Controllers/.gitkeep
   src/ReplicatedStorage/Binders/Shared/.gitkeep
   src/ReplicatedStorage/Binders/Client/.gitkeep
   ```

   Every folder a boot script names must exist or the boot script errors. Git drops empty folders, so keep
   the `.gitkeep` files (Rojo ignores them).

`InitServer.server.luau`:

```lua
--!strict
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local Init = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Init)

Init.start({
	{ Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Network } },
	{
		Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Services, ServerScriptService.Services },
		Predicate = Init.matchesName("Service$"),
	},
	{ Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Binders.Shared, ServerScriptService.Binders } },
}):andThen(function()
	workspace:SetAttribute("ServerStarted", true)
end)
```

`InitClient.client.luau`:

```lua
--!strict
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local Init = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Init)

Init.start({
	{ Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Network } },
	{ Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Services }, Predicate = Init.matchesName("Service$") },
	{ Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Controllers }, Predicate = Init.matchesName("Controller$") },
	{ Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Binders.Shared, ReplicatedStorage.Binders.Client } },
})
```

Rojo file names: `Name.luau` is a ModuleScript, `Name.server.luau` a Script, `Name.client.luau` a
LocalScript, a folder with `init.luau` is a ModuleScript with children, `Name.model.json` is any instance.
Attributes go in `Name.meta.json`: `{ "attributes": { "Priority": -10 } }`.

## 2B. Install in Studio

Best for the user: install the **Init Framework** plugin
(https://create.roblox.com/store/asset/77164672536940/Init-Framework), then press **Setup** (loader, boot
scripts and folders) and **Add Packages** (Trove, Signal, Packet, Binder). Ask the user to do this; you
can't click plugin buttons. Studio's Assistant can't download files, so this is its only way to install.

If you can run Luau in Studio (`execute_luau`) and read and write the user's files but the plugin isn't an
option:

1. Get `Init.rbxm` from https://github.com/KashTheKing/init/releases/latest.
2. Copy it into Studio's content folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\Versions\<version>\content\` on Windows,
   `RobloxStudio.app/Contents/Resources/content/` on macOS) and run
   `game:GetObjects("rbxasset://Init.rbxm")[1]` in edit mode, or ask the user to drag the file into the
   Explorer.
3. Put the `Init` ModuleScript in `ReplicatedStorage.Packages` (make the folder if needed).
4. Create Script `InitServer` in ServerScriptService and LocalScript `InitClient` in
   StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts with the boot script sources from 2A, and these Folders:
   `ReplicatedStorage.{Network, Services, Controllers, Binders.Shared, Binders.Client}`,
   `ServerScriptService.{Services, Binders}`.

## 3. Add modules

Read the template, replace every `_SNIPPET_` with the **base name** (no suffix), and save it under the full
module name. The boot scripts only load names that match their predicate, so **the suffix matters**:
`Service.luau` with `_SNIPPET_` = `Shop` gives a module named `ShopService`.

| You want | Template | `_SNIPPET_` | Module name | Goes in (Rojo file in the layout above) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Server game logic | `Service.luau` | `Shop` | `ShopService` | ServerScriptService.Services (`src/ServerScriptService/Services/ShopService.luau`) |
| Logic on server and client | `Service.luau` | `Time` | `TimeService` | ReplicatedStorage.Services (`src/ReplicatedStorage/Services/TimeService.luau`) |
| Client game logic | `Controller.luau` | `Camera` | `CameraController` | ReplicatedStorage.Controllers (`src/ReplicatedStorage/Controllers/CameraController.luau`) |
| One ScreenGui | `GuiController.luau` | the ScreenGui's name, `Shop` | `ShopGuiController` | ReplicatedStorage.Controllers |
| Remote events (Packet) | `Network.luau` | `Shop` | `ShopNetwork` | ReplicatedStorage.Network |
| Code per tagged instance | `Binder.luau` | the tag, `Lava` | `LavaBinder` | ServerScriptService.Binders (server), ReplicatedStorage.Binders.Client or .Shared |
| An object class | `Class.luau` | `Weapon` | `Weapon` | ReplicatedStorage.Classes (Init doesn't load it; `require` it) |
| A subclass | `InheritedClass.luau` | `Sword` | `Sword` | child of the parent class's ModuleScript (`Classes/Weapon/init.luau` + `Classes/Weapon/Sword.luau`) |
| A class per bound instance | `BoundClass.luau` | `Lava` | `Lava` | child of its Binder (`Binders/LavaBinder/init.luau` + `Lava.luau`); the Binder does `Binder.new(require(script.Lava), { Tags = { "Lava" } })` |
| Player input | `Input.model.json` | (none) | `CombatInput` | ReplicatedStorage.Input (`src/ReplicatedStorage/Input/CombatInput.model.json`); set the Keyboard binding's `KeyCode` |

In Studio, create a ModuleScript with that name and the filled template as its `Source` (for
`Input.model.json`, create the InputContext, InputAction and InputBindings it describes).

Network, Binder and BoundClass need packages, as `ReplicatedStorage.Packages.<Name>`. Rojo: add
`Packet = "kashtheking/packet@1.0.0"`, `Binder = "kashtheking/binder@0.6.3"`, `Trove = "sleitnick/trove@1.8.0"`
to `wally.toml` and `wally install`. Studio: the plugin's **Add Packages**.

## 4. Rules that matter

- **Init**: set up the module's own state. Runs one module at a time; don't wait for other modules or
  yield for long (3 s `InitTimeout`, then the module is reported and skipped).
- **Start**: runs after every Init has finished, so other modules are ready. All Starts run at once; a Start
  that waits doesn't block the others (15 s `StartTimeout`, then Init stops waiting; the Start keeps running).
- To use another module, `require` it (from the top of the file or inside Start). It returns the same table
  Init loaded. Don't call its methods during your Init.
- Hooks (all optional): `OnPlayerAdded(player)` (also runs for players already in game),
  `OnPlayerRemoving(player)`, `Step(dt)` (fixed 60/s), `OnHeartbeat(dt)`, `OnStepped(time, dt)`; client only:
  `OnRenderStepped(dt)`, `OnCharacterAdded(character)`, `OnCharacterRemoving(character)`, `OnDied()`.
  Never connect `Players.PlayerAdded` yourself in an Init module; use the hook.
- A ModuleScript inside another ModuleScript is not loaded by Init. Put private helpers there.
- Every module must `return` exactly one value. Module names should be unique across loaded folders.
- Attributes on a ModuleScript: `Ignore = true` skips it; `Priority = <number>` loads it earlier (lower first)
  within its entry.
- Never call `Init.start` anywhere except the two boot scripts.
- To load another folder, add an entry to **both** boot scripts if it's shared:
  `{ Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Systems }, Predicate = Init.matchesName("System$") }`, and create the folder.

## 5. Check it works

- **Rojo**: `rojo build <project>.project.json -o build.rbxl` must succeed (it catches bad file names and
  project paths). Run `selene` and `luau-lsp analyze` if the project has them. Then the user runs
  `rojo serve`, connects from Studio and presses Play; ask them for the Output.
- **Studio**: start a playtest and read the Output.

The Output should show:

```
🔲 Initializing Server
✅ Initialized 4 Server modules in 0.02s
🔲 Initializing Client
✅ Initialized 3 Client modules in 0.01s
```

Errors start with `[Init]` and name the module and method. Common ones:
- `X is not a valid member of ReplicatedStorage`: a folder named in a boot script is missing. Create it.
- `must return exactly one value`: the module has no `return` at the end.
- `X:Init() didn't finish within 3s`: Init is waiting on something; move that into Start.
- A module never runs: its name doesn't match the entry's predicate (e.g. `Shop` instead of `ShopService`),
  it's nested inside another ModuleScript, or it has the `Ignore` attribute.
- More: https://kashtheking.com/init/docs/guides/troubleshooting/

## Templates

### Binder.luau

```lua
--!strict
-- A Binder (kashtheking/binder): runs code for every instance with a tag, and cleans up when it goes away.
-- Install Trove and Binder from Wally or the plugin's "Add Packages".
-- Put it in ServerScriptService/Binders (server), ReplicatedStorage/Binders/Client (client) or
-- ReplicatedStorage/Binders/Shared (both). Init calls the binder's Start for you.
-- This example pushes every part tagged "_SNIPPET_" forward at its "Speed" attribute.
-- Binder docs: https://kashtheking.com/library/docs/packages/binder
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Binder = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Binder)
local Trove = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Trove)

-- Called for each matching instance. The trove is cleaned when the instance is unbound;
-- anything you return with a :Destroy() method is cleaned too.
local function _SNIPPET_(part: BasePart, trove: Trove.Trove, speed: number)
	trove:Connect(RunService.Heartbeat, function()
		part.AssemblyLinearVelocity = part.CFrame.LookVector * speed
	end)

	return trove
end

return Binder.new(_SNIPPET_, {
	Tags = { "_SNIPPET_" }, -- instances need one of these CollectionService tags
	ClassNames = { "BasePart" }, -- and must be one of these classes (optional)
	Ancestors = { workspace }, -- and must be inside one of these (optional)

	-- Last check (optional). Return true to bind; anything returned after true goes to the constructor.
	Predicate = function(instance: Instance)
		local speed = tonumber(instance:GetAttribute("Speed"))
		if not speed then
			warn(`[_SNIPPET_Binder] {instance:GetFullName()} needs a number "Speed" attribute`)
			return false
		end
		return true, speed
	end,
})
```

### BoundClass.luau

```lua
--!strict
-- A class for a Binder to construct, one per bound instance: Binder.new(_SNIPPET_, { Tags = { "_SNIPPET_" } }).
-- Put it next to the Binder that uses it. The Binder cleans the trove when the instance is unbound.
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local Trove = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Trove)

local _SNIPPET_ = {}
_SNIPPET_.__index = _SNIPPET_

export type _SNIPPET_Properties = {
	Instance: Instance,
	Trove: Trove.Trove,
}

export type _SNIPPET_ = typeof(setmetatable({} :: _SNIPPET_Properties, _SNIPPET_))

export type ClassType = _SNIPPET_

-- Called by the Binder for each bound instance. Values your Binder's Predicate returns after `true`
-- arrive as extra parameters after the trove.
function _SNIPPET_.new(instance: Instance, trove: Trove.Trove): _SNIPPET_
	local self = setmetatable(
		{
			Instance = instance,
			Trove = trove,
		} :: _SNIPPET_Properties,
		_SNIPPET_
	)

	return self
end

-- Called by the Binder when the instance is unbound
function _SNIPPET_.Destroy(self: _SNIPPET_): () end

return _SNIPPET_
```

### Class.luau

```lua
--!strict
-- A plain class (an object you make many of with .new). Init does NOT load classes; require them yourself.
-- Put it in ReplicatedStorage/Classes (shared) or ServerScriptService/Classes (server-only).
local _SNIPPET_ = {}
_SNIPPET_.__index = _SNIPPET_

export type _SNIPPET_Properties = {}

export type _SNIPPET_ = typeof(setmetatable({} :: _SNIPPET_Properties, _SNIPPET_))

export type ClassType = _SNIPPET_

-- Creates a new _SNIPPET_
function _SNIPPET_.new(): _SNIPPET_
	local properties: _SNIPPET_Properties = {}

	local self = setmetatable(properties, _SNIPPET_)

	return self
end

-- Cleans up the _SNIPPET_
function _SNIPPET_.Destroy(self: _SNIPPET_): () end

return _SNIPPET_
```

### Controller.luau

```lua
--!strict
-- A Controller: client-only game logic that Init loads and starts for you. Name it <Something>Controller.
-- Put it in ReplicatedStorage/Controllers. Every method below is optional; delete the ones you don't use.
local _SNIPPET_Controller = {}

export type _SNIPPET_Controller = typeof(_SNIPPET_Controller)

-- Runs first, one module at a time. Set up this module's own state here.
-- Don't wait for other modules here (they may not have run Init yet); use Start for that.
function _SNIPPET_Controller.Init(self: _SNIPPET_Controller) end

-- Runs after every module's Init has finished. Safe to use other modules here.
-- Waiting here is fine for a few seconds (StartTimeout is 15s); it doesn't hold up other modules.
function _SNIPPET_Controller.Start(self: _SNIPPET_Controller) end

---- Runs for the local player's current character, then every time it respawns
--function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnCharacterAdded(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, character: Model)
--
--end

---- Runs when the local player's character is being removed
--function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnCharacterRemoving(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, character: Model)
--
--end

---- Runs when the local player's Humanoid dies
--function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnDied(self: _SNIPPET_Controller)
--
--end

---- Runs every frame before it renders (camera, UI that follows things)
--function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnRenderStepped(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, dt: number)
--
--end

---- Runs for every player already in the game (the local player too), then for every player who joins
--function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnPlayerAdded(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, player: Player)
--
--end

---- Runs when a player is leaving the game
--function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnPlayerRemoving(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, player: Player)
--
--end

---- Runs exactly 60 times a second, however fast the frames are
--function _SNIPPET_Controller.Step(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, dt: number)
--
--end

---- Runs every RunService.Heartbeat
--function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnHeartbeat(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, dt: number)
--
--end

return _SNIPPET_Controller
```

### GuiController.luau

```lua
--!strict
-- A Controller for one ScreenGui. Name the ScreenGui in StarterGui "_SNIPPET_" (or change the name below).
-- Put it in ReplicatedStorage/Controllers. It's a normal Controller with the GUI lookup done for you.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local player = assert(Players.LocalPlayer, "_SNIPPET_GuiController must be required on the client")
local PlayerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui") :: PlayerGui

-- Gives you autocomplete for the ScreenGui's children (works when the ScreenGui exists in StarterGui)
export type Gui = typeof(game:GetService("StarterGui")["_SNIPPET_"])

local _SNIPPET_GuiController = {
	Gui = (nil :: any) :: Gui,
}

export type _SNIPPET_GuiController = typeof(_SNIPPET_GuiController)

-- The ScreenGui is copied into PlayerGui when the player spawns, which can take a moment, so wait for it in Start
function _SNIPPET_GuiController.Start(self: _SNIPPET_GuiController)
	self.Gui = assert(
		PlayerGui:WaitForChild("_SNIPPET_", 5) :: any,
		`[_SNIPPET_GuiController] the ScreenGui "_SNIPPET_" didn't appear in PlayerGui`
	)
end

return _SNIPPET_GuiController
```

### InheritedClass.luau

```lua
--!strict
-- A class that inherits from another class. Insert it as a child of the parent class's ModuleScript.
-- Init does NOT load classes; require them yourself.
local SuperClass = require(script.Parent)

local _SNIPPET_ = setmetatable({}, SuperClass)
_SNIPPET_.__index = _SNIPPET_

export type _SNIPPET_ = typeof(_SNIPPET_) & SuperClass.ClassType & {
	__super: SuperClass.ClassType,
}

export type ClassType = _SNIPPET_

-- Creates a new _SNIPPET_; arguments go to the parent class's .new
function _SNIPPET_.new(...: any): _SNIPPET_
	local super = SuperClass.new(...)

	local self: _SNIPPET_ = setmetatable(super :: any, _SNIPPET_) :: any
	self.__super = super

	return self
end

return _SNIPPET_
```

### Input.model.json

```json
{
	"className": "InputContext",
	"properties": {
		"Priority": 1000,
		"Sink": false
	},
	"children": [
		{
			"name": "InputAction",
			"className": "InputAction",
			"properties": {
				"Type": "Bool"
			},
			"children": [
				{ "name": "Mouse", "className": "InputBinding", "properties": { "KeyCode": "MouseLeftButton" } },
				{ "name": "Keyboard", "className": "InputBinding" },
				{ "name": "Gamepad", "className": "InputBinding", "properties": { "KeyCode": "ButtonR2" } },
				{ "name": "Touch", "className": "InputBinding" }
			]
		}
	]
}
```

### Network.luau

```lua
--!strict
-- Network packets, made with kashtheking/packet (install it from Wally or the plugin's "Add Packages").
-- Put it in ReplicatedStorage/Network. Init loads Network first on both sides, so every packet exists
-- before anything sends one. Docs: https://kashtheking.com/library/docs/packages/packet
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local Packet = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Packet)

return {
	-- Packet.new(name, ...types). Use exact types (Packet.NumberU8, Packet.String, ...) for smaller packets.
	_SNIPPET_ = Packet.new("_SNIPPET_", Packet.Any),
}
```

### Service.luau

```lua
--!strict
-- A Service: game logic that Init loads and starts for you. Name it <Something>Service.
-- Server-only: ServerScriptService/Services. Shared (runs on server AND client): ReplicatedStorage/Services.
-- Every method below is optional; delete the ones you don't use.
local _SNIPPET_Service = {}

export type _SNIPPET_Service = typeof(_SNIPPET_Service)

-- Runs first, one module at a time. Set up this module's own state here.
-- Don't wait for other modules here (they may not have run Init yet); use Start for that.
function _SNIPPET_Service.Init(self: _SNIPPET_Service) end

-- Runs after every module's Init has finished. Safe to use other modules here.
-- Waiting here is fine for a few seconds (StartTimeout is 15s); it doesn't hold up other modules.
function _SNIPPET_Service.Start(self: _SNIPPET_Service) end

---- Runs for every player already in the game, then for every player who joins
--function _SNIPPET_Service.OnPlayerAdded(self: _SNIPPET_Service, player: Player)
--
--end

---- Runs when a player is leaving the game
--function _SNIPPET_Service.OnPlayerRemoving(self: _SNIPPET_Service, player: Player)
--
--end

---- Runs exactly 60 times a second, however fast the frames are (good for game ticks)
--function _SNIPPET_Service.Step(self: _SNIPPET_Service, dt: number)
--
--end

---- Runs every RunService.Heartbeat
--function _SNIPPET_Service.OnHeartbeat(self: _SNIPPET_Service, dt: number)
--
--end

---- Runs every RunService.Stepped (before physics)
--function _SNIPPET_Service.OnStepped(self: _SNIPPET_Service, time: number, dt: number)
--
--end

return _SNIPPET_Service
```


---


# What is Init?

Init is a **module loader**: the thing that starts your game's code.

Without one, every Script runs on its own, in an order you don't control, and each one connects `Players.PlayerAdded`, `RunService.Heartbeat` and friends by hand. With Init, your game has exactly two scripts (one for the server, one for the client) and everything else is a ModuleScript in a folder:

```
ReplicatedStorage
├─ Packages/Init            the loader
├─ Network                  remote events (loaded first)
├─ Services                 code for server AND client   (names end in Service)
├─ Controllers              code for the client only     (names end in Controller)
└─ Binders/Shared, Client   code that runs per tagged instance
ServerScriptService
├─ InitServer               boots the server
├─ Services                 server-only code              (names end in Service)
└─ Binders
StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts
└─ InitClient               boots the client
```

When the game starts, Init:

1. **Loads** every module, folder by folder, in the order the boot script lists them.
2. Calls **`Init`** on each one, one at a time. Modules set up their own data here.
3. Calls **`Start`** on all of them. Now every module is ready, so they can use each other.
4. Connects their **hooks**: `OnPlayerAdded`, `OnPlayerRemoving`, `Step` (60 times a second), `OnHeartbeat`, and on the client `OnCharacterAdded`, `OnDied`, `OnRenderStepped`...

A module only writes the methods it needs:

```lua
local CoinService = {}

function CoinService.Init(self)
	self.Coins = {}
end

function CoinService.OnPlayerAdded(self, player: Player)
	self.Coins[player] = 0
end

function CoinService.OnPlayerRemoving(self, player: Player)
	self.Coins[player] = nil
end

return CoinService
```

## Pick how to install

- **[Without code](install/no-code.md):** the Init Framework plugin. Two clicks.
- **[With AI](install/with-ai.md):** paste one prompt into Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT.
- **[Rojo + Wally](install/wally.md):** `kashtheking/init`.
- **[Studio, by hand](install/model.md):** drag in `Init.rbxm`.

Next: [the lifecycle](guides/lifecycle.md) explains exactly when each method runs.


---


# Install without code

The **Init Framework** plugin sets up everything. You don't need to write a line.

1. Get the plugin from the Creator Store: [Init Framework](https://create.roblox.com/store/asset/77164672536940/Init-Framework). In Studio it appears in the **Plugins** tab.
2. Open your place and press **Setup**. This adds:
   - the loader at `ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Init`
   - `InitServer` in ServerScriptService and `InitClient` in StarterPlayer › StarterPlayerScripts
   - the folders: `Network`, `Services`, `Controllers`, `Binders`, `Classes`, `Constants`, `Input`
3. Press **Add Packages** for Trove, Signal, Packet and Binder (the Network and Binder templates use them).
4. Press **Play**. The Output shows `✅ Initialized 0 Server modules` and `✅ Initialized 0 Client modules`. Init is running.

## Add your first module

1. Click the `Services` folder in **ServerScriptService**.
2. Press **Service** in the plugin. A new module opens.
3. Rename it in the Explorer to `Coin`. The plugin renames it `CoinService` and fills the name into the code.
4. Write your code in the methods (delete the ones you don't need) and press Play.

Every button works the same way: select the folder, press the button, rename.

| Button | Makes | Put it in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Service | game logic (`...Service`) | ServerScriptService › Services (server) or ReplicatedStorage › Services (both) |
| Controller | client logic (`...Controller`) | ReplicatedStorage › Controllers |
| Gui Controller | a controller for one ScreenGui | ReplicatedStorage › Controllers |
| Network | Packet remote events | ReplicatedStorage › Network |
| Binder | code for every part with a tag | ServerScriptService › Binders, ReplicatedStorage › Binders › Client or Shared |
| Bound Class | a class for a Binder | next to the Binder |
| Class / InheritedClass | an object class | ReplicatedStorage › Classes |
| Input | an InputContext | ReplicatedStorage › Input |
| Add Extras | an `Assets` folder that preloads, plus SFX and Music sound groups | |
| Update Script Name | renames the open script to the text you selected | |

What every template does: [Templates](../guides/templates.md).

:::tip Let an AI write the modules
Once Setup is done, an AI can add modules for you. See [Install with AI](with-ai.md).
:::


---


# Install with AI

Init ships an **AI skill**: one file that teaches an AI how to install Init (in a Rojo project or in Studio), where every kind of module goes, the rules to follow, and every template. Point your AI at it.

- Skill, with every template inside: [`https://kashtheking.com/init/SKILL.md`](https://kashtheking.com/init/SKILL.md)
- Templates (raw): `https://kashtheking.com/init/templates/Service.luau`, `Controller.luau`, `Binder.luau`, ...
- Everything in one page for AI: [`https://kashtheking.com/init/llms.txt`](https://kashtheking.com/init/llms.txt)

## Copy this prompt

Paste it into Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT or any AI that can read web pages:

```text
Read https://kashtheking.com/init/SKILL.md and follow it.
Set up the Init framework (kashtheking/init) in my Roblox game, then add a CoinService
that gives every player 100 coins when they join and shows them on the leaderboard.
```

Change the second part to whatever you want built. After setup, you can keep asking: *"add a ShopGuiController for my Shop ScreenGui"*, *"add a LavaBinder that kills players who touch parts tagged Lava"*.

## Claude Code

Install the plugin once and Claude uses the skill whenever you mention Init. It carries the templates, so it works offline:

```text
/plugin marketplace add KashTheKing/init
/plugin install init@kashtheking-init
```

In a Rojo project, Claude edits files and runs `wally install`. With the **Roblox Studio MCP** connected, it can create the modules in Studio and playtest.

## Roblox Studio's Assistant

Studio's built-in Assistant can't read web pages, so give it the skill once:

1. Open [`kashtheking.com/init/SKILL.md`](https://kashtheking.com/init/SKILL.md), select everything (Ctrl+A) and copy it.
2. In Studio's Assistant, type `Save this as a skill named init-framework:` and paste.

It shows up under the Assistant's **Skills** tab and is used whenever you ask for Init things. The Assistant can't install plugins, so press **Setup** in the [plugin](no-code.md) yourself first.

## Cursor, Codex and other coding AIs

In a Rojo project with Init installed by Wally, the skill and templates are on disk at `Packages/_Index/kashtheking_init@<version>/init/skills/init/SKILL.md` and `.../init/templates/`. Add one line to your `AGENTS.md` (or `.cursor/rules`):

```text
This game uses the Init framework. Before changing modules, read Packages/_Index/kashtheking_init@*/init/skills/init/SKILL.md.
```

## If your AI can't touch Studio or files

Chat AIs (ChatGPT, Claude.ai) can't click in Studio. Do the setup with the [plugin](no-code.md) (two clicks), then ask the AI for module code and paste it into a module the plugin made.

## Check the AI's work

Press Play. The Output should say `✅ Initialized N Server modules` and `✅ Initialized N Client modules`. Anything that starts with `[Init]` is an error: paste it back to the AI. See [Troubleshooting](../guides/troubleshooting.md).


---


# Install with Rojo + Wally

1. Add Init to `wally.toml`:

   ```toml
   [dependencies]
   Init = "kashtheking/init@1.0.1"
   ```

2. `wally install`, and map `Packages` to `ReplicatedStorage.Packages` in your project file.

3. Add the boot scripts and folders. The [example project](https://github.com/KashTheKing/init/tree/main/example) has all of them; copy it, or start from it:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/KashTheKing/init && cd init && rojo serve example.project.json
   ```

   - [`ServerScriptService/InitServer.server.luau`](https://github.com/KashTheKing/init/blob/main/example/ServerScriptService/InitServer.server.luau)
   - [`StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/InitClient.client.luau`](https://github.com/KashTheKing/init/blob/main/example/StarterPlayerScripts/InitClient.client.luau)

   Every folder a boot script names must exist. Git doesn't keep empty folders, so add a `.gitkeep` to each (Rojo ignores it) or declare them in the project file with `"$className": "Folder"`.

4. `rojo serve`, connect from Studio and press Play.

Your folders, names and order are yours: change the entries in the boot scripts. See [Entries](../guides/entries.md).

The [templates](../guides/templates.md) are plain `.luau` files you can copy (Wally also puts them in `Packages/_Index/kashtheking_init@<version>/init/templates/`), and the [plugin](no-code.md)'s template buttons work in Rojo games too.


---


# Install by hand in Studio

1. Download `Init.rbxm` from the [latest release](https://github.com/KashTheKing/init/releases/latest).
2. In Studio, make a Folder named `Packages` in ReplicatedStorage. Drag `Init.rbxm` onto it (or right-click it › **Insert from File**).
3. Make a **Script** named `InitServer` in ServerScriptService and paste in [InitServer](https://github.com/KashTheKing/init/blob/main/example/ServerScriptService/InitServer.server.luau).
4. Make a **LocalScript** named `InitClient` in StarterPlayer › StarterPlayerScripts and paste in [InitClient](https://github.com/KashTheKing/init/blob/main/example/StarterPlayerScripts/InitClient.client.luau).
5. Make the folders the boot scripts name: in ReplicatedStorage `Network`, `Services`, `Controllers`, `Binders` (with `Shared` and `Client` inside); in ServerScriptService `Services` and `Binders`.
6. Press Play and look for `✅ Initialized` in the Output.

The [plugin](no-code.md)'s Setup button does all of this for you.


---


# Lifecycle

`Init.start(entries)` runs in this order, separately on the server and on each client.

## 1. Load

Entries load in list order. Inside an entry, every ModuleScript in its `Folders` (at any depth) is required, lowest `Priority` attribute first, then in Explorer order. Skipped:

- a ModuleScript inside another ModuleScript (it belongs to its parent, which can `require` it)
- a module whose `Ignore` attribute is `true`
- a module the entry's `Predicate` turns down (e.g. not ending in `Service`)

A module that errors while loading is reported and left out; the rest still load.

## 2. Init: one at a time

`module:Init()` runs for each module, in load order, and Init waits for each before the next. Use it for the module's **own** setup: tables, constants, instances it owns. Other modules may not have run their Init yet, so don't call into them here.

If Init errors or takes longer than `InitTimeout` (3 s), it's reported and **that module doesn't Start** or get hooks.

## 3. Start: all at once

After every Init has finished, `module:Start()` runs for every module, in load order, each in its own thread. A Start that waits (for a GUI, for data) doesn't hold up the others. This is where modules use each other.

If Start errors or runs longer than `StartTimeout` (15 s), it's reported. A Start that's still running keeps running; Init just stops waiting for it.

## 4. Hooks

As soon as a module's Start returns, its hooks connect:

| Method | Runs | Args |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OnPlayerAdded` | for each player already in game, then each player who joins | `player` |
| `OnPlayerRemoving` | when a player leaves | `player` |
| `Step` | exactly 60 times a second, however fast frames run | `dt` (1/60) |
| `OnHeartbeat` | every `RunService.Heartbeat` | `dt` |
| `OnStepped` | every `RunService.Stepped` | `time, dt` |
| `OnRenderStepped` | client: every frame before render | `dt` |
| `OnCharacterAdded` | client: local player's current and each new character | `character` |
| `OnCharacterRemoving` | client: when the character is removed | `character` |
| `OnDied` | client: when the local player's Humanoid dies | |

Errors in a hook are reported and don't break the event. Per-frame hooks get a MicroProfiler label like `CoinService - Step`.

## 5. Done

The promise from `Init.start` resolves once every Start has returned (or timed out):

```lua
Init.start(entries):andThen(function(modules, count, seconds)
	print(modules.CoinService, count, seconds)
end)
```

## Using one module from another

Modules are plain tables, and `require` returns the same table Init loaded:

```lua
local CoinService = require(ServerScriptService.Services.CoinService)

function ShopService.Start(self)
	CoinService:Give(player, 10) -- fine: every Init has run
end
```


---


# Entries and folders

The boot scripts decide what loads and in what order. Each entry is a group of folders:

```lua
Init.start({
	{ Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Network } },                     -- 1st: every module in Network
	{
		Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Services, ServerScriptService.Services },
		Predicate = Init.matchesName("Service$"),                      -- 2nd: only names ending in Service
	},
	{ Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Binders.Shared, ServerScriptService.Binders } }, -- 3rd
})
```

- **Order:** entries load in list order. Inside an entry, the `Priority` attribute (lower first) then Explorer order.
- **Predicate:** a function `(module) -> boolean`. `Init.matchesName(pattern)` makes one from a [string pattern](https://create.roblox.com/docs/luau/strings#string-patterns): `"Service$"` ends in Service, `"^Admin"` starts with Admin.
- **Shared folders** (in ReplicatedStorage) go in **both** boot scripts.

## Adding your own folder

Say you want `ReplicatedStorage.Systems` with modules named `...System`:

1. Make the folder.
2. Add an entry to `InitServer` and `InitClient` (or just one, if it's one-sided):

   ```lua
   { Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Systems }, Predicate = Init.matchesName("System$") },
   ```

## Attributes

Set these on a ModuleScript in the Properties window:

| Attribute | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Ignore` | boolean | `true`: Init skips it |
| `Priority` | number | lower loads earlier inside its entry (default 0) |

## The old Entries modules

The old Init kept entries in `SharedEntries`/`ServerEntries`/`ClientEntries` modules as named dictionaries with `Order`. That format still works: `Init.start(require(path.to.ServerEntries))` sorts it by `Order`. See [Migrating](../migrating.md).


---


# Settings

Pass overrides as the second argument of `Init.start`. A name that isn't a setting is an error, so typos are caught.

```lua
Init.start(entries, { Verbose = true, StartTimeout = 30 })
```

| Setting | Default | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Verbose` | `false` | log every module as it loads, inits and starts |
| `DefaultLogEnabled` | `true` | log `🔲 Initializing` and `✅ Initialized N modules` |
| `DebugLabelFormat` | `"%s - %s"` | MicroProfiler label for per-frame hooks (module, method) |
| `InitTimeout` | `3` | seconds to wait for each `Init` |
| `StartTimeout` | `15` | seconds to wait for each `Start` |
| `DefaultPriority` | `0` | priority of modules without a `Priority` attribute |
| `IgnoreAttribute` | `"Ignore"` | attribute that skips a module |
| `PriorityAttribute` | `"Priority"` | attribute that orders modules |

The method names are settings too, if you'd rather call them something else:

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `InitMethod` | `"Init"` |
| `StartMethod` | `"Start"` |
| `PlayerAdded` | `"OnPlayerAdded"` |
| `PlayerRemoving` | `"OnPlayerRemoving"` |
| `Accumulator` | `"Step"` |
| `Heartbeat` | `"OnHeartbeat"` |
| `Stepped` | `"OnStepped"` |
| `RenderStepped` | `"OnRenderStepped"` |
| `Died` | `"OnDied"` |
| `CharacterAdded` | `"OnCharacterAdded"` |
| `CharacterRemoving` | `"OnCharacterRemoving"` |

Source: [`Settings.luau`](https://github.com/KashTheKing/init/blob/main/src/Init/Settings.luau).


---


# Troubleshooting

Init's errors start with `[Init]` and name the module and method.

| You see | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Network is not a valid member of ReplicatedStorage` | a boot script names a folder that doesn't exist | make the folder, or remove the entry |
| `... must return exactly one value` | the module doesn't end with `return` | add `return MyModule` at the bottom |
| `X:Init() didn't finish within 3s` | Init is waiting (WaitForChild, a DataStore, another module) | move the waiting into `Start` |
| `X:Start() didn't finish within 15s` | Start waits a long time | fine if intended (it keeps running); otherwise `task.spawn` the loop or raise `StartTimeout` |
| `X:Init() errored: ...` | a bug in Init | fix it; that module won't Start until then |
| `Two loaded modules are named "X"` | two modules share a name | rename one; both still run |
| `Init.start was already called` | two boot scripts on one side | keep one InitServer and one InitClient (the old `ReplicatedStorage.Init` boots too, see [Migrating](../migrating.md)) |
| `"X" isn't a setting` | a typo in the settings table | check [Settings](settings.md) |

## A module never runs

- Its name doesn't match the entry's predicate: `Coins` isn't loaded by `matchesName("Service$")`; name it `CoinService`.
- It's inside another ModuleScript. Only top-level modules (folders are fine) load.
- It has the `Ignore` attribute.
- It's in a folder no entry lists, or on the wrong side (a Controller in ServerScriptService).
- Turn on `Verbose = true` to see every module Init loads.

## Nothing prints at all

The boot scripts aren't running: `InitServer` must be a **Script** in ServerScriptService and `InitClient` a **LocalScript** in StarterPlayerScripts, both enabled.


---


# Migrating from the old Init

The old Init was a ModuleScript at `ReplicatedStorage.Init` with `Settings`, `SharedEntries`, `ServerEntries`, `ClientEntries` and two scripts inside it that booted the game. Your modules don't change: same `Init`, `Start` and hook methods.

1. Press **Setup** in the [plugin](install/no-code.md) (or [install by hand](install/model.md)). It adds `ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Init`, `InitServer` and `InitClient`.
2. If you changed the old Entries modules, copy those folders into the new boot scripts as list entries (`Order` becomes the position in the list). If you changed `Settings`, pass those values as the second argument of `Init.start`.
3. Delete `ReplicatedStorage.Init`. While it's there, it boots the game a second time.
4. Press Play and check for `✅ Initialized`.

## What behaves differently

- **Every Init runs before any Start.** The old loader ran Init then Start per module, so a Start could run before other modules' Init. If a Start relied on that, move the code into Init.
- **Starts run at the same time.** A slow Start no longer holds up the modules after it.
- **Modules run in the order you list.** The old loader required in order but called Init/Start in an arbitrary order.
- **Modules inside a ModuleScript aren't loaded.** The old one loaded them too, unless a predicate filtered them out.
- **`Step` runs at 60 per second.** The old one read `Stepped`'s first argument (the game time) as the frame time, so it could run many extra steps per frame.
- **A timed-out Init or Start keeps running.** The old one cancelled it.
- Start errors are always reported (the old one only reported them with `Verbose`).
